response.content:
## Defence and Drone Companies That Expanded to Norway in 2026

Based on available reporting through November 2026, several defence and drone companies have expanded their presence or deepened partnerships in Norway:

### Companies Joining NORDSEC (Nordic Defence and Security Cluster) in Norway

- **Knightec** — A Swedish engineering firm with roots in Kongsberg Våpenfabrikk, bringing decades of defence, maritime, and engineering expertise to Norway's NORDSEC cluster (announced November 2026).
- **Aviant** — A Norwegian drone company specialising in autonomous logistics and ISR (intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance), which joined NORDSEC to contribute long-range drone expertise (November 2026).
- **Emblem Automekanikk AS** — Joined NORDSEC as a new member (November 2026).
- **Keystones** — Brought recruitment and engineering expertise to NORDSEC (November 2026).

### Defence-Industrial Partnerships Expanding into Norway

- **Teledyne FLIR Defense** (US) — Announced a partnership with **STORM** from Oslo, Norway (July 2026) to integrate its Black Recon drone-in-a-box reconnaissance system into STORM's modular RADS vehicle platform, expanding Teledyne FLIR's drone operations footprint in Norway.
- **DevDroid** (Ukraine) — Signed a memorandum of understanding with **Inission Norge AS** (Norway) to co-produce remote-control systems for ground robotic systems for the defence forces of Norway and Ukraine, exploring full production and assembly of electronics in Norway under the "Drone Deal" cooperation model.
- **Saronic Technologies** (US) — While not establishing a Norwegian office, the autonomous vessel company awarded a $100 million+ contract to Norway's Syncrolift (Nekkar ASA) in November 2026 for the world's largest shiplift, deepening its ties with Norwegian defence-maritime industry.

### Broader Context

- The **Atlantic Future Forum** was held in Oslo in November 2026, co-hosted by the UK and Norway, drawing over 50 political, military, and industry leaders and catalysing new defence-industrial partnerships.
- **UFORCE** (Ukrainian-founded, UK-headquartered drone company) demonstrated its combat-proven autonomous vessels from HMS Prince of Wales in Norwegian waters, with plans to support Northern European allies through the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF).
- **Kongsberg Maritime** (Norway) launched the unmanned vessel **Arctic Hunter** as part of the UK's Type 92 programme for submarine tracking in the Far North.
- Norway and the UK formalised a £90 million deal for three mine-hunting drone motherships under the P1118 programme, further integrating their defence-industrial bases.

The NORDSEC cluster and Norway's long-term defence plan (approximately $60 billion over 12 years) have been key magnets for both established defence primes and emerging drone companies expanding into the Norwegian market in 2026.

Ukrainian ground robotic system manufacturer DevDroid has signed a memorandum of understanding with Norwegian electronics and electronic systems company Inission Norge AS. **Details:** The manufacturers plan to collaborate to produce remote-control systems for the defence forces of Norway and Ukraine. They will also explore the possibility of establishing a full production and assembly cycle for electronics. "Together with our partners, we are exploring the possibility of cooperation under the Drone Deal, a model of long-term defence cooperation between Ukraine and partner countries based on the exchange of technology and experience," DevDroid said. Under the memorandum, DevDroid and Inission Norge AS will also explore opportunities for the joint development and production of defence systems. # UK to buy three new mine-hunting drone motherships under Norway agreement

The decision, for which £90 million ($119.1 million) has been allocated, was formalized on Thursday by British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and his Norwegian counterpart, Tore O. Sandvik, at the Atlantic Future Forum in Oslo.

By Elisabeth Gosselin-Malo  on November 13, 2026 9:16 am

Share Options

Share a link to this article

 Email
 Facebook

 X

 

The UK will buy three counter-mine "motherships" from Norway under a new agreement. (UK Ministry of Defence) [...] MILAN — The UK this week formalized plans to purchase three new mine-hunting “motherships” that can deploy unmanned mine countermeasure assets, as part of a defense cooperation agreement with Norway.

Under the UK-Norway Lunna House Agreement, signed last December, the British government announced its intention to join the Norwegian P1118 Standardized Vessel Program to develop offshore support vessels as motherships for autonomous mine-hunting systems.

The decision, for which £90 million ($119.1 million) has been allocated, was formalized on Thursday by British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and his Norwegian counterpart, Tore O. Sandvik, at the Atlantic Future Forum in Oslo. [...] “This deal strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy…[We are] using the biggest sustained increase in defense spending since the Cold War to put the latest modern technology in the hands of our sailors,” Streeting said.

The British Ministry of Defense said the vessels, built on the same family as Norway’s naval version of the P1118 design, will help keep sailors “further from danger” and, as a result, support “anti-submarine warfare capabilities on NATO’s northern flank.”

The first ship is expected to arrive in 2031, and the deal includes an option for London to order three more.

The investment is a shining example of the UK-Ukraine 100 Year Partnership, deepening the defence industrial relationship between the two countries and bringing combat-proven Ukrainian technology to Britain.

### Oliver Holbourn, Chief Executive Officer of the National Wealth Fund, said: [...] UFORCE is a Ukrainian-founded, UK-headquartered defence technology company developing combat-proven autonomous and uncrewed systems across sea, land and air.

The investment will significantly expand UFORCE’s presence across the UK, creating hundreds of high-skilled jobs in engineering, software, artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing. The UK will serve as a base to support allies, like the nations of the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF), with a particular focus on capabilities for operating in Northern seas.

The United Kingdom will order three new mine-hunting drone motherships from Norway as part of bilateral defense cooperation. [...] In addition to mine countermeasures missions, these platforms will become part of the Royal Navy’s hybrid fleet concept and will support anti-submarine operations on NATO’s northern flank.

The procurement will take place through the intergovernmental Maritime Capability Partnership Framework (MCPF), and the UK defense investment plan has allocated an additional €107 million for this project.

This agreement is part of a broader defense partnership accompanying the contract to export British Type 26 frigates to Norway, valued at approximately €12 billion, which was signed in December 2025.

The use of identical platforms by both countries is intended to enhance interoperability between the British and Norwegian navies during joint operations in the North Atlantic. [...] The launched frigate HMS Glasgow heads to dry dock in Scotstown. Photo credits: BAE Systems

At the same time, a number of other naval programs were presented at the forum in Oslo, including the Atlantic Net contract worth over €107 million between the British Ministry of Defense and Ocean Infinity for the deployment of autonomous systems to monitor underwater threats.

Earlier, the Norwegian company Kongsberg Maritime launched the unmanned vessel Arctic Hunter.

The drone was developed based on a civilian Arctic-class vessel as part of the UK’s Type 92 program. Its primary mission is to search for and track submarines in the challenging conditions of the Far North.
